# Djuli

> Djuli is a cloud-based scientific data management and analysis platform built by Zimmer & Peacock (ZP). It is designed for storing, analysing and sharing electrochemical, biosensor and in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) data, with first-class support for ZP's SenseItAll (SIA) hardware and any third-party instrument that can export common data formats.

## What Djuli does

- Stores raw sensor data in user-owned **clusters** and **projects**.
- Runs reproducible analyses (amperometry, potentiometry, voltammetry, impedance, spatial mapping) with configurable preprocessing, fitting and statistical evaluation.
- Generates shareable **reports** combining metadata, raw plots, processed plots and analytics (R^2, LoB/LoD/LoQ, model coefficients).
- Supports collaboration via shared reports, reviewer assignment and custom templates.
- Exposes a REST API so IoT devices and external scripts can push data and pull results.

## Who it is for

- Electrochemists, biosensor developers and IVD researchers.
- Hardware integrators using SenseItAll, FoodSense, or other ZP instruments.
- Teams that need traceable data analysis with an audit trail per data point.

## Key concepts

- **Cluster** - top-level workspace owned by a user. Groups related projects.
- **Project** - a folder of related reports within a cluster.
- **Report** - one experiment: metadata (operator, equipment, protocol), the raw files used, the analysis configuration, the produced plots and the analytics.
- **Study** - the analysis applied inside a report. Each study type has its own preprocessing and fitting options.
- **Cluster / Project / Report tree** - the navigation sidebar in the web app.
- **Contextual help** - hover-driven help panel inside the web app; its content lives in [github.com/djuliZP/djuli-documentation](https://github.com/djuliZP/djuli-documentation).

## Supported study types

Discrete (one measurement per concentration / sample):

- Amperometry (AD)
- Potentiometry (PD)
- Voltammetry (VD)
- Impedance / EIS
- Spatial mapping

Continuous (time-series):

- Amperometry (AC)
- Potentiometry (PC)
- Generic Continuous (GC)

Users can also create a Generic study when their workflow does not match a predefined type.

## Supported data formats

CSV, XLSX, JSON, XML, PSSession, MTD, TRM, DT6, TXT/DB, and media files (PNG and others). Direct streaming from ZP hardware is also supported.

## Preprocessing tools

Crop, baseline adjustment, BPF / BSF / HPF / LPF filters, median filter, moving average, Savitzky-Golay smoothing, flip, offset, extrapolate, accumulate, differentiate, outlier detection.

## Analysis tools

Equation fitting, statistical extraction (per-line and global), standard addition, feature check, delta fit, mean fit, peak fit (position / height / area under curve), spatial mapping.

## Hardware integration

- **SenseItAll (SIA)** - ZP's portable potentiostat family. Streams data directly into Djuli.
- **FoodSense** - ZP's portable food-analysis instrument (capsaicin / Scoville, gingerol, caffeine); ships with Djuli Premium included.
- **Third-party instruments** - any device that exports a supported file format works.
- **Public REST API** - push data from IoT devices, pull results into external dashboards.

## Pricing

- **Freemium** - free tier; signup at https://dju.li/register
- **Premium** - paid tier with additional storage, API access and team features. Buyers of SenseItAll or FoodSense hardware get Premium included: the account is upgraded automatically the first time the user logs into the SIA / FoodSense companion app with the same email and password they use on Djuli.
